solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arrange insurance and head for shelter

definitions.meaning: to take out cover is to buy an insurance policy
to duck out of rain or gunfire into somewhere safe

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out a policy and then runs from the storm.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves sound like a sequence of errands, but each is a complete meaning of the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking cover means both buying insurance and sheltering from danger.

clue.text: Sadly lost ring in workman's gear

indicators.note: things done sadly are done badly, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A workman mourns a wedding ring that has vanished somewhere in his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring reads as jewellery; in wordplay a ring is almost always the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the gear a tradesman carries is the kit he works with.

clue.text: Captures youngster and dozes

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a child and then nods off, an oddly calm criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole answer is spelt out in the clue: the thing seized plus the snooze that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap someone is to capture them and hold them.

clue.text: Protection from officer by end of day — and no mistake

parts.note: a cop is a police officer

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: what is right contains no mistake

explanation.surface: A policeman offers protection by nightfall, and he means it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Protection' looks like police business, which is why 'officer' sits beside it; the answer is legal protection for creative work.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyright protects authors and artists from having their work copied.

clue.text: Portuguese explorer at first very assured skinning fish and lizard

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the three words that follow

parts.note: the three words whose first letters are taken
the cod is a common food fish
an agama is an Old World lizard, often brightly coloured

explanation.surface: A very confident fishmonger skins a fish and a lizard, as if preparing for a voyage of discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinning' looks like an operation on the fish, but it is only the third word giving a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Vasco da Gama was the Portuguese navigator who first sailed from Europe to India round the Cape of Good Hope.

clue.text: Found in cage in tribunal

indicators.note: the answer sits in the next word

parts.note: the letters sit just after the T, inside the word

explanation.surface: Something discovered in a prisoner's cell during a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cage' suggests a prison, but it is the ribcage; the definition is a description, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribs are the bones that make up the ribcage.

clue.text: European's address from individuals backing Republican

indicators.note: going backwards: the word is read right to left

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A political speech given by a European, with people rallying behind a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' means a form of address, not a speech or a street: Señor is Spanish for Mr or sir.
explanation.definitionFit: Señor is how a Spanish man is addressed, the equivalent of Mr.

clue.text: Notes first of rays coming from the sun

parts.note: SO and LA, two notes of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone jots down notes on the first sunbeams of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests writing, but here it is two musical notes from do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the Latin sol, sun, as in solar power or the solar wind.

clue.text: Rain spoilt outside broadcast, one at African capital

indicators.note: something spoilt is damaged out of its proper shape, so the letters of rain are rearranged

parts.note: OB is the broadcasting abbreviation for an outside broadcast
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Rain ruined an outside broadcast being made in an African capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoilt' rearranges RAIN to NAIR; OB is TV shorthand for a programme made on location.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya, in East Africa.

clue.text: They haven't won, but have a drink with athlete

explanation.surface: Losing competitors console themselves with a drink alongside an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' only places the two pieces side by side, so the athlete can come first though the clue names the drink first.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: those who finish second, or lower, in a contest are by definition not the winners.

clue.text: Dictionary (American) includes one page on tragic figure

indicators.note: the outer pieces hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: An American dictionary gives a single page to a figure from Greek tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make 'American' look like a description of the dictionary, but it is its own piece, and the dictionary and the nationality together wrap round 'one page'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the king of Sophocles' play, who unknowingly kills his father and marries his mother, is the classic tragic hero.

clue.text: Gold signs overlap

indicators.note: the two words share the letter where they meet, so one copy of L is dropped

parts.note: the Bull (Taurus), a sign of the zodiac; its final L is shared

explanation.surface: Stock-market indicators for gold run into one another.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'signs', supplies two zodiac signs, and 'overlap' tells you BULL and LION share their L.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: the word means precious metal in bulk bars, and gold is the usual example.

clue.text: Steps look sound

definitions.note: 'Stair' can mean a whole flight of steps, so the plural clue word fits

indicators.note: say the word and listen to it

parts.note: to stare is to look hard

explanation.surface: An instruction to check that some steps are safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look sound' reads as 'seem solid'; instead 'sound' tells you to say a word for 'look' out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair, or a flight of stairs, is a set of steps.

clue.text: Beating snooper up intentionally

indicators.note: a beating knocks things about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone beat up a spy, and they meant to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like part of the phrase 'beating up', but it is fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an adverbial phrase meaning deliberately, with intent.

clue.text: In trouble, prophesy about church's response

indicators.note: one word goes round another

parts.note: the congregation's reply to a prayer

explanation.surface: A prophet foresees how a church will respond to trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In trouble' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'trouble'. PREDIC-AMEN-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tight spot or awkward situation is trouble.

clue.text: Had been noticed, on return

definitions.note: 'Was' and 'had been' are close past forms of 'be', not an exact swap

indicators.note: going back: the word is read right to left

explanation.surface: Someone had been spotted on their way back.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a report from a lookout; 'on return' is the instruction to turn SAW around.
explanation.definitionFit: Was and had been are both past forms of the verb to be.

clue.text: Who is Fred? Badly desired!

indicators.note: the letters are put together badly, out of order

explanation.surface: Nobody knows who Fred is, yet he is badly wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark tries to split the clue into two sentences; 'Badly desired' reads as 'wanted very much', but 'Badly' belongs to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are past participles for something longed for.

clue.text: Prague first ordered citrus foods

indicators.note: put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In Prague, a diner orders the fruit course first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as a restaurant order, which suits the food.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the large sour breakfast fruit is one of the citrus family.

clue.text: Ian Fleming character reviewed Blake Bros.

indicators.note: viewed again in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic reviews a firm called Blake Brothers for a Bond book.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosa Klebb is the SMERSH villain with the poisoned shoe blade in From Russia with Love.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of many characters in the James Bond novels.

clue.text: Strange Tuscan sign for churches?

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so the letters of Tuscan are put out of their order

parts.note: Aries, the ram, is the first sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An odd Tuscan sign is pointing the way to the local churches.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: churches are one kind of sanctuary, places of refuge or holy places.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctuary is a holy place, and churches have traditionally offered sanctuary to fugitives.

clue.text: Streamlined housing getting energy from sodium battery first

indicators.note: the pieces before it go at the front

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sleek new house draws its power from a sodium battery above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing' suggests homes, but a nacelle houses an engine. 'First' puts NA CELL ahead of the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is the streamlined casing around an aircraft engine.

clue.text: Sleep in khaki pyjamas

indicators.note: the answer is inside the words that follow

parts.note: the last two letters of the first word run into the first letter of the second

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps in army-coloured nightwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Kip is informal British for a sleep or nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: informal British slang for a sleep or nap.

clue.text: Cocky type, 22, was almost captured

indicators.note: the second piece has been captured inside the first

explanation.surface: A cocky type was nearly caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to KNOLL; KNO(WA)LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is a cocky person who thinks they know everything.

clue.text: Woman cuddling baby, eating a hot snack

indicators.note: a cuddle wraps arms round someone, so the woman goes round the baby
what is eaten goes inside, so the baby holds A

explanation.surface: A woman holds her baby while eating a hot snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest, innermost first: the baby eats 'a', and the woman then cuddles the result. Ena is a stock crossword woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a tortilla filled and baked in a hot chilli sauce.

clue.text: Peaceful girl, alluring one, topless, at end of promenade

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means the top, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: a siren is an alluring woman, after the singers of Greek myth who lured sailors

indicators.note: at end of picks out the last letter of the next word

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A peaceful girl, an alluring one, goes topless at the far end of the seaside promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' in the surface is a sunbather; in the wordplay it drops the S from SIREN. The name comes from the Greek for peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene derives from the Greek eirene, meaning peace, and Eirene was the Greek goddess of peace.

clue.text: Hillock seen returning from hill on Kerrera

indicators.note: the answer can be seen inside the words
going back: read right to left

explanation.surface: A little mound spotted on the way back from a hill on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerrera is a small island off Oban in western Scotland; its name matters only for its K.
explanation.definitionFit: A knoll is a small rounded hill, a hillock.

clue.text: Sports car for such idle eaters

definitions.meaning: a British make of sports car, founded by Colin Chapman
in the Odyssey, an island people who ate a fruit and forgot all wish to go home

explanation.surface: A fast car wasted on people who only sit about eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such idle eaters' asks which word goes before 'eaters': the lotus-eaters, who forgot home after eating the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a brand name for a car; the other is the flower whose fruit Homer's idle eaters lived on.

clue.text: Those lumberjack chaps!

definitions.meaning: the surface reads this as pointing at some lumberjacks; the setter means people who cut down trees
the surface reads this as a cheery 'those guys!'; the setter means an informal word for men

explanation.surface: An admiring exclamation about some lumberjacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer means both tree-fellers and chaps, so the lumberjacks are fellers twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumberjacks fell trees, and fellers is a colloquial word for men.

clue.text: I am Caesar's dim follower. Problem?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Latin word for 'I am', the language Julius Caesar spoke
second meaning: the word that comes after 'dim' to name the Cantonese dumpling dish
third meaning: an arithmetic exercise set in school, a problem to work out

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings: 'dim follower' sounds like a slow-witted disciple of Caesar, but it asks for the word that comes after 'dim' in a familiar phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is Latin for 'I am' (as in cogito ergo sum), completes the Chinese dish dim sum, and names an arithmetic exercise.

clue.text: Graceful and neat, oddly concealing limb

indicators.note: the rearranged word conceals the limb, holding it inside
oddly means in an odd way, so the letters of neat are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone graceful and neat strangely keeps a leg hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' could suggest taking odd letters, but here it is the anagram signal; the shuffled word splits round the limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means stylish and refined in movement or appearance, a close synonym of graceful.

clue.text: Bird will change course back by far end of lake

indicators.note: back means the word for changing course is read backwards

parts.note: to veer is to change course; will just makes it a future verb in the surface

indicators.note: far end of takes the final letter of lake

explanation.surface: A bird flying back over a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve is the female of the ruff, a wading bird.

clue.text: Postpones work on the two arcades, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford don famous for swapping the first sounds of words, signals that the opening consonants are exchanged

parts.note: malls are shopping arcades, said aloud as MAWLZ; the Spoonerism swaps the opening sounds of the two spoken words

explanation.surface: A council postpones work on both shopping arcades, as the Reverend Spooner might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'According to Spooner' swaps the opening B and M of BOTH MALLS, giving MOTH BALLS.
explanation.definitionFit: To mothball a project is to put it into storage and postpone work on it until later.
